paper.title: xxHash algorithm specification, XXH64 (xxhash_spec.md version 0.2.0)
paper.venue: xxHash project specification and sanity test vectors (not peer reviewed)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm description in the specification; no third-party code copied. The known-answer data is in vectors_seed0.inc and vectors_seed1.inc (numbers only)
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: XXH64 with seed 0 of the first n bytes of the project's pseudo-random test buffer outputs the 4161 published digests for every n = 0..4160
XXH64 with seed 0x9E3779B1 outputs the 4161 published digests for the same inputs (8322 digests in all)
the inputs cover every tail length, the short-input path, the stripe loop and the accumulator convergence

expected_values_source.what: the XSUM_XXH64_testdata array of the project's sanity vectors (length, seed, digest), and the buffer generator XSUM_fillTestBuffer in the xsum_sanity_check.c next to it; the algorithm is from the specification
expected_values_source.note: the vectors are data, copied as numbers by a script that also checked their order (length ascending, seeds 0 then 0x9E3779B1); the project's code was not copied

negative_control: built with XXH64_ROT=30 (rotation in the stripe round 30 instead of 31), only the 8 shortest inputs per seed (lengths 0 to 7, which never reach a stripe round) still match, 8 of 4161 for each seed, and the program exits 1
not_checked: the streaming (incremental) interface and inputs longer than 4160 bytes
the other xxHash members (XXH3, XXH128) and seeds other than 0 and 0x9E3779B1
dispersion or collision-quality claims, and speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about real hardware)
big-endian hosts; the program reads input as little-endian bytes as the specification requires
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 8322 digests the xxHash project publishes for XXH64. It does not show anything about hash quality.
